checks.finding: Core terms (EXCLUSIVE/OVERLAP/UNOWNED/SHARED bounded-unbounded, EXCLUDED_MATCH, disabled-legacy/advisory/required derived states, glob semantics, NFC-vs-raw-identity, case sensitivity) all have a dedicated Field Definitions entry and matching AC/TEST coverage. No residual term found that two implementers would reasonably resolve differently.

requirements.md REQ-004/AC-033 was edited this round to make an adapter_paths glob match against an EXCLUSIVE-owned changed path the sole Fail-6 trigger, explicitly stating 'no additional per-binding facet or revision field is defined.' investigation.md's OQ-001 'Resolved' section was not updated and still states Fail-6 triggers only when the glob matches a diff path 'without the corresponding binding facet/revision also present in the diff' -- the exact clause requirements.md just removed as undefined. This leftover phrase exists only at investigation.md's OQ-001 section, contradicting requirements.md's corrected text. Because requirements.md's own Dependencies section cites investigation.md as the source of OQ-001's resolution, an implementer or design reviewer following investigation.md would build an extra facet/revision-absence check that no longer exists in the schema, producing a materially different Fail-6 trigger than REQ-004/AC-033/TEST-033 specify. This is an in-package contradiction between two reviewed Phase 1 artifacts over a fail-closed coverage-gate trigger condition, not an implementation-policy question, and meets the Critical bar for a direct requirement/investigation-claim conflict.

Acceptance tests cover material negative/empty/boundary/failure paths individually: unsupported-metacharacter rejection, empty diff and empty-include-list error, NFC-collision fail-closed, schema-absence fail-closed, exclude-as-include invariant, unresolvable-rev/unrelated-histories fail-closed, invalid-UTF-8 path fail-closed, renameLimit-exceeded fail-closed, submodule/symlink fixtures, TOCTOU retry-then-fail-closed, manifest-missing hard error, provider-bindings-file-absent N/A+WARN, and cross-epic template-absent fail-closed.

The Assumptions section ties each cross-epic/tooling assumption to either a fail-closed conformance fixture or an explicit deferred-dependency note rather than a silent guess. OQ-002 documents the adopted middle-path decision explicitly rather than leaving it open. OQ-001 is marked resolved with a concrete rule (though its investigation.md restatement is stale -- see CONTRADICTION).

Roles and Permissions defines a testable human-approval boundary: the implementing agent never writes a protected path directly and stages every protected-file candidate under human-copy/; the human maintainer performs cp + SHA-256 verification for guard-invariants.json, its generated siblings, check-contract.{sh,ps1,py}, and .github/workflows/test.yml; Approval Draft to Approved is a human-only action. AC-036/AC-041/AC-047/AC-051 give concrete, checkable pass/fail conditions for this irreversible-change boundary.

requirements.md/acceptance-tests.md are internally self-consistent (aside from the investigation.md contradiction flagged above) and map every REQ to concrete, individually-IDed AC/TEST pairs with explicit fail-closed behavior, so a design reviewer can proceed from REQ-004/AC-033's own text without inventing Fail-6's trigger rule. Resolving the flagged CONTRADICTION (updating investigation.md to match) is the one outstanding blocker before handoff.
